title: the compile reads a block's engine traces into a deterministic floor
intention: cairn.machines.learning_block.compile reads one block's training engine_run traces and emits a floor: data a deterministic Python evaluator runs to reproduce each traced decision (winner or escalation) from the run's recorded input and candidates, with no inference; it refuses, naming every lack, a corpus too thin or too featureless to generalize from.
why: Child 2 of d6cacb63868b (infer-compile-reads-the-traces): its cast condition, >=5 training-typed traces for one block, is met (librarian-ask, 7). But measured 2026-11-13, those 7 are one question repeated 4 times plus 3 backfill escalations, and no candidate record carries the provides the constraints judged. A compile over that corpus could only memorize. So the engine must record features first, and the compile must refuse a corpus that only repeats itself.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel: a settled block decision compiles to code instead of re-running inference) and Law 8 (a compile that memorizes must not pass for one that learned).
how: D1: run_block's candidates_log keeps each candidate's provides. D2: compile.py's compile_floor(block, *, holder, root=None) reads the block's training engine_run traces, refuses (DoorRefused, every lack) fewer than 5 runs of distinct input or any candidate without provides, and otherwise emits a floor of per-constraint kill rules over provides keys plus the decide-or-escalate order; apply_floor(floor, payload, candidates) evaluates it. The floor berths under the holder that compiled it, at ~/.cairn/devices/<holder>/<n>/machines/learning_block/floors/<block>.json (outline 16.4.3; CLAUDE.md, a held machine's state hangs off its holder). D3: the proof, over a scratch trace root. Built red-first; held at BUILDME by Q#97 (which corpus the first compile learns from).

clauses.claim: over a scratch trace root holding >=5 engine runs of one block with distinct inputs, compile_floor emits a floor, and apply_floor reproduces every traced run's outcome (winner name or escalation target) from that run's recorded input and candidates
two compiles over the same corpus write byte-identical floors, and compile.py imports no inference client

compile_floor refuses, naming every lack in one refusal, a corpus with fewer than 5 runs of distinct input and a corpus whose candidates carry no provides; a fixture shaped like the live librarian-ask corpus as measured 2026-11-13 is refused on both
a run_block over a fixture spec writes each candidate's provides into candidates_log, and the existing engine teeth in test_learning_block.py stay green

decisions.text: D1: engine.py run_block's candidates_log entry gains 'provides': the candidate's provides dict exactly as _satisfies judged it.

D2: new compile.py: compile_floor(block, *, holder, root=None) and apply_floor(floor, payload, candidates). Reads training engine_run traces through the engine's trace root; refuses via DoorRefused with every lack; emits per-constraint kill rules keyed on provides values plus the escalation target; writes the floor under its holder, instance_path(<holder device>, <n>)/machines/learning_block/floors/<block>.json, holder given as '<device>/<n>' (e.g. 'librarian/0'), refused (DoorRefused) when absent or unparseable, sorted keys, no timestamps in the body.
D3: proof test_the_compile_reads_the_traces.py, one tooth per clause, every trace and floor under a scratch root (the world() pattern of test_learning_block.py).

Q#97 read as outline 16.1.3 says: the runs whose candidates something killed teach (each kill's provides + killed_by gives an allow-list per separating provides key; several separating keys are all required, which can only escalate more, never answer wrongly); every run is the agreement check and a floor that cannot reproduce its corpus is refused; an unseen value is killed so a fresh task escalates. The one refusal also names: no kill anywhere, escalation targets != 1, and a constraint no provides key separates (rule:<name>, e.g. a fact-judged constraint).
decisions.step: unlisted: the floor learns from the kills

out: the floor's deposit into a graph tree (outline 4.3.1.4), cast once a floor exists

measured.saw: librarian-ask holds 7 engine_run training traces; 4 of them are one question ('Is CC allowed to seal concept-pieces on its own?') with one winner, 0:5a34fcee46b7, every time; the other 3 are backfill runs (backfills=3, reason 'learned'), all 3 escalated to the operator, carries_his_answer killing 5, 6 and 5 of their 6 candidates; every candidates_log entry carries only name, outcome, killed_by and outranked_by, no provides
measured.how: read ~/.cairn/devices/learning_block/0/traces/librarian-ask.jsonl line by line (Linux, akiendell), and survey_the_corpus() from cairn/machines/learning_block/probes/engine_trace_corpus.py: librarian-ask 7 runs, 7 answer all five; intentions_model_compiler 2 runs

measured.saw: engine.py builds candidates_log from name, outcome, killed_by, outranked_by (cairn/machines/learning_block/engine.py run_block); the candidate's provides, the only features _satisfies reads, is dropped from the record
